issues.description: The problem statement uses two different method names for the animal feeding sound (messageOnFeed() in the UML and earlier descriptions, but getFeedingSound() in later task descriptions and in the feedAllAnimals() explanation). The solution and intended template structure use messageOnFeed(), while parts of the problem text instruct students to call/get getFeedingSound(). This name/signature inconsistency will confuse students about which method to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Either (A) update the problem statement to always refer to messageOnFeed() (and change examples mentioning getFeedingSound() to messageOnFeed()), or (B) change the solution/template to expose getFeedingSound() (or provide a clear alias) and update UML/docs accordingly. Ensure feedAllAnimals() and singFarmSong() examples use the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement uses two different identifiers for the same concept of an animal's feeding sound: messageOnFeed() (declared in the UML and described in Part 1) and getFeedingSound() (used in Part 2 and in the song template). The solution and intended implementation use messageOnFeed(), but the mixed naming in the problem statement (and the song text) can confuse students about which method to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent identifier across all artifacts. Prefer messageOnFeed() (as declared in the UML and implemented in the solution). Update the problem statement and the song template to replace all occurrences of getFeedingSound() with messageOnFeed(), and clarify example song lines to call animal.messageOnFeed(). Alternatively, if getFeedingSound() is preferred, rename the abstract method and all usages in template/solution consistently to getFeedingSound().
